title: Planner: local custom fields on plan tasks
summary: The briefing accurately reports the launched feature, Microsoft's rollout notice and the documented governance routes. It preserves the difference between the licensing sources and distinguishes blocking the Teams app from the broader Planner PowerShell control.

claims.quote: Custom Fields let you tailor your plans to match the way your team works.

claims.claim: The field types are Text, Number, Date, Yes/No and Choice.
claims.quote: Add Text, Number, Date, Yes/No, and Choice fields to capture the information that matters most.

claims.claim: Learn and the notice name no role specifically responsible for managing local custom fields.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner custom fields admin role; Planner local custom fields tenant admin enable disable Set-PlannerConfiguration custom fields role management. Opened Planner for admins, service description, Graph customFieldDefinition and export-user-data; read MC1492955. No managing role found.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no tenant-wide UI or API switch specifically for Planner local custom fields.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner local custom fields tenant admin enable disable Set-PlannerConfiguration; Planner custom fields disable Graph. Opened Planner for admins, disable-planner, manage-planner-app and Graph customFieldDefinition. Found whole-app controls and read APIs, not a custom-field tenant switch.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search reaches audit search.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal.
Select the Audit solution card.
On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog searches audit records and does not restrict custom fields.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog. That means you can use this cmdlet to search the audit log instead of using the search tool on the Audit page in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Audit search needs the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log. ... To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog must be run in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: You have to run this cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Planner > Block turns off the Planner app.
claims.quote: In the left pane of the Teams admin center, go to Teams apps > Manage apps. ... To turn off Planner for your organization, search for the Planner app, select it, and then select Block.

claims.claim: Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false is the documented Planner on/off command.
claims.quote:
Turn off Planner for your organization using PowerShell
Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false
To turn on Planner back:
Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $true

claims.claim: The Planner tenant-admin PowerShell command requires a global admin.
claims.quote: If you're a global admin and you want to turn off Microsoft Planner for your organization, you can use Windows PowerShell.

claims.claim: The Teams admin center Block action governs the Planner app in Teams.
claims.quote: Planner is enabled by default for all Teams users in your organization. You can turn off or turn on the app at the org level on the Manage apps page in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The PowerShell page covers basic plans in Teams and Web and all plans in other Planner endpoints.
claims.quote:
This article applies to:
- Basic plans in the Planner app in Teams and Web
- All plans in other Planner endpoints (including Planner mobile, and Planner connectors).

claims.claim: The last row gives coarse Planner availability controls, not a switch specifically for custom fields.
claims.quote: If you're a global admin and you want to turn off Microsoft Planner for your organization, you can use Windows PowerShell.

claims.claim: Custom field edits are logged in Task History.
claims.quote: Custom field edits are logged in Task History and flow to the Unified Audit Log.

claims.claim: Custom field edits flow to the Unified Audit Log and can be monitored as task-edit activity.
claims.quote: Custom field edits are logged in Task History and flow to the Unified Audit Log. ... custom field activity appears in audit logs like other task edits.
